image-alt.label: Images with no alternative text
image-alt.why: Screen-reader users hear a file name or nothing, so they miss what the image shows or does.
image-alt.fix: Add an alt attribute that describes the image's purpose. If the image is purely decorative, use an empty alt (alt="").
image-alt.shopify: In the admin, open the product, select the image and add alt text. In theme code, `{{ product.featured_image | image_url: width: 800 | image_tag }}` outputs the alt text saved in the admin. For decorative images use `alt=""`.

input-image-alt.label: Image buttons with no alternative text
input-image-alt.why: An image used as a button needs text that says what the button does.
input-image-alt.fix: Give <input type="image"> an alt attribute such as alt="Search".
input-image-alt.shopify: Search-icon buttons in themes are often image or SVG buttons. Add alt or a visually hidden label.

color-contrast.label: Text that is hard to read against its background
color-contrast.why: Low-contrast text is hard to read for people with low vision, and for everyone in bright light.
color-contrast.fix: Normal text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background. Large text (about 24px, or 18.66px bold) needs 3:1. Darken the text or lighten the background.
color-contrast.shopify: In the theme editor, change the colour scheme so text and background meet the ratios. For a quick fix, add a CSS override in your theme's custom CSS box, for example `.price { color: #4a4a4a; }`, then re-check.

label.label: Form fields with no label
label.why: Screen-reader users cannot tell what to type, and a placeholder is not a label.
label.fix: Connect every field to a visible <label for="id"> or, if the design has no visible label, a visually hidden label.
label.shopify: Newsletter and search fields are common offenders. Add `<label for="Email" class="visually-hidden">Email</label>` before the input and define `.visually-hidden { position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden; clip:rect(0 0 0 0); white-space:nowrap; }` if your theme lacks it.

select-name.label: Dropdowns with no label
select-name.why: A dropdown without a label is announced only as 'combo box', so users cannot tell what it chooses.
select-name.fix: Add a <label for> pointing to the <select>, or an aria-label.
select-name.shopify: Sort-by and variant dropdowns in themes need a label. Use a visually hidden label like the one for form fields.

link-name.label: Links with no readable text
link-name.why: Icon-only or empty links are announced as 'link', so users cannot tell where they go.
link-name.fix: Give every link text, or an aria-label for icon-only links, for example aria-label="Instagram".
link-name.shopify: Social-media icons in the footer and cart icons in the header are the usual cause. Add `aria-label="Instagram"` to the <a> or visually hidden text inside it.

button-name.label: Buttons with no readable text
button-name.why: An icon-only button is announced only as 'button'.
button-name.fix: Add visible text or aria-label to each button, for example aria-label="Open cart".
button-name.shopify: Menu toggles, close buttons and quantity steppers are common. Add an aria-label that says what the button does.

html-has-lang.label: Page language not set
html-has-lang.why: Screen readers pick a voice and pronunciation from the page language. Without it they may read English text with the wrong voice.
html-has-lang.fix: Add a lang attribute to the <html> element, for example <html lang="en">.

html-lang-valid.label: Page language value is invalid
html-lang-valid.why: A malformed language code is ignored by assistive technology.
html-lang-valid.fix: Use a valid BCP 47 code such as en, en-US or fr.

document-title.label: Page has no title
document-title.why: The title is the first thing a screen reader announces and what appears in browser tabs and search results.
document-title.fix: Give every page a unique, descriptive <title>.
document-title.shopify: In theme.liquid the head should contain `<title>{{ page_title }}</title>`.

meta-viewport.label: Page blocks pinch-zoom
meta-viewport.why: Low-vision users on phones rely on zooming. Blocking it makes the page unusable for them.
meta-viewport.fix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1 from the viewport meta tag.
meta-viewport.shopify: Use `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` in theme.liquid.

frame-title.label: Embedded frames with no title
frame-title.why: Screen-reader users cannot tell what an embedded video, map or widget is.
frame-title.fix: Add a title attribute to every <iframe> that describes its content.
frame-title.shopify: Review embeds in apps and in custom HTML sections, and add `title="Product video"` or similar.

video-caption.label: Videos with no captions
video-caption.why: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users cannot follow video without captions.
video-caption.fix: Add a captions track: <track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">.
video-caption.shopify: For YouTube or Vimeo embeds, upload captions on the video platform. For self-hosted video add a <track> element.

link-in-text-block.label: Links inside text distinguished by colour alone
link-in-text-block.why: Users who cannot see colour differences cannot find the links.
link-in-text-block.fix: Underline links inside body text, or add another visual cue with at least 3:1 contrast.
link-in-text-block.shopify: Add `.rte a { text-decoration: underline; }` (or your theme's rich-text class) in custom CSS.

target-size.label: Tap targets that are too small
target-size.why: Small buttons and links are hard to hit for people with motor impairments, and on phones.
target-size.fix: Make interactive targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or space them so a 24px circle around each does not overlap another.
target-size.shopify: Check footer links, quantity steppers and carousel dots. Add padding to the clickable element.

aria-allowed-attr.label: ARIA attribute not allowed on this element
aria-allowed-attr.why: Wrong ARIA can make a control announce incorrectly, which is often worse than none.
aria-allowed-attr.fix: Remove the attribute, or change the element or role so the attribute is valid.
aria-allowed-attr.shopify: Often comes from an app or a theme section. Identify the element in the plan's examples and remove or correct the attribute.

aria-required-attr.label: ARIA role missing a required attribute
aria-required-attr.why: Some roles need extra attributes to work with assistive technology.
aria-required-attr.fix: Add the attribute the role requires, or remove the role.
aria-required-attr.shopify: Often from a custom slider or tab widget. Check the element listed in the examples.

aria-valid-attr-value.label: ARIA attribute has an invalid value
aria-valid-attr-value.why: A broken reference (for example aria-labelledby pointing to an id that does not exist) leaves the control unnamed.
aria-valid-attr-value.fix: Correct the value, or make sure the id it points to exists.
aria-valid-attr-value.shopify: IDs generated in Liquid loops can collide or go missing. Check that referenced ids render.

aria-roles.label: Invalid ARIA role
aria-roles.why: An unknown role is ignored, so the element loses its meaning.
aria-roles.fix: Use a valid role, or better, a native HTML element.

aria-hidden-focus.label: Hidden content can still be focused
aria-hidden-focus.why: Keyboard users can land on elements that screen readers are told to ignore.
aria-hidden-focus.fix: Do not put focusable elements inside aria-hidden regions, or remove them from the tab order.
aria-hidden-focus.shopify: Common with off-canvas menus and cart drawers that are hidden visually but still focusable. Add the `inert` attribute while they are closed.

label-content-name-mismatch.label: Visible button or link text differs from its accessible name
label-content-name-mismatch.why: People using voice control say what they see on screen, such as "click Add to cart". If the hidden name is different, the command fails.
label-content-name-mismatch.fix: Make the aria-label start with the exact visible text, or remove the aria-label so the visible text is used.
label-content-name-mismatch.shopify: Common on product cards and header buttons where an aria-label such as "Open cart drawer" replaces visible text like "Cart". Change it to start with the visible word, for example aria-label="Cart, open drawer".

nested-interactive.label: Controls nested inside other controls
nested-interactive.why: A button or link inside another button or link is announced unpredictably, and keyboard users may not reach the inner one.
nested-interactive.fix: Do not put interactive elements inside other interactive elements. Restructure so they are siblings.
nested-interactive.shopify: Often a product card where the whole card is a link and contains an add-to-cart button. Make the card a container and link only the title or image.

aria-prohibited-attr.label: ARIA attribute not allowed on this element
aria-prohibited-attr.why: Some elements cannot carry a name, so an aria-label on them is ignored or announced inconsistently.
aria-prohibited-attr.fix: Move the attribute to a suitable element, add an appropriate role, or remove it.
aria-prohibited-attr.shopify: Often an aria-label on a plain <div> or <span> added by a theme or app. Put the label on a link, button or region instead.

aria-input-field-name.label: Custom input with no accessible name
aria-input-field-name.why: A custom dropdown, slider or search box with a role but no name is announced without saying what it is for.
aria-input-field-name.fix: Add aria-label or aria-labelledby to the element with the input role, or use a native <input> or <select> with a <label>.
aria-input-field-name.shopify: Typical of search-as-you-type widgets and filter sliders from apps. Add aria-label="Search products" or a visible label.

aria-required-parent.label: ARIA element missing its required parent
aria-required-parent.why: Some roles only work inside a specific container, for example a tab must sit inside a tablist.
aria-required-parent.fix: Wrap the element in the required parent role, or remove the role.
aria-required-parent.shopify: Often from custom tabs, menus or carousels. Check the structure of the widget listed in the examples.
